newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM TO BACK FRENCH JOBS DRIVE AT AMSTERDAM TALKS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM TO BACK FRENCH JOBS DRIVE AT AMSTERDAM TALKS.

text.p: At the EU summit in Amsterdam early next week Belgium will back France in its drive to focus the single currency project more on jobs, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Saturday.

"During the Maastricht Treaty negotiations there was agreement to develop not only the monetary aspect but also to coordinate other aspects of economic policy," Mastadt said in an interview with financial daily L'Echo.
"The French government rightly underlines that this coordination cannot be limited to budget policy, but must include other aspects such as employment," he added.

He said that in Amsterdam EU leaders would have to agree on a text which summarises this idea. Maystadt also said he backed the idea of a "council for the coordination of economic policies" where countries taking part in the single currency could coordinate their economic policies.
He also said that France was not questioning the need for a stability pact as such, in particular the need to maintain budget discipline after the advent of the euro.
